question: Which of the following semi-solid pharmaceutical forms with which a master formula can be prepared has greater occlusivity ?:

CHAIN: "Hydrophilic or ole-aqueous creams" -> "high water content" -> "less effective barrier" -> "lower occlusivity" -> 60%

enhanced_information: Hydrophobic ointments are characterized by high lipid content, which allows them to form a strong barrier on the skin, resulting in greater occlusivity compared to other formulations. This aligns with the consensus that occlusivity is primarily influenced by lipid content. Hydrophobic or water-oily creams, while containing both water and oil, provide moderate barrier formation and thus have less occlusivity than hydrophobic ointments. Hydrophilic or ole-aqueous creams, with their high water content, are less effective at forming a barrier, leading to lower occlusivity. Finally, hydrophilic ointments, being primarily water-based, exhibit minimal barrier effect and the lowest occlusivity. Therefore, the order of occlusivity from highest to lowest is: hydrophobic ointments > hydrophobic or water-oily creams > hydrophilic or ole-aqueous creams > hydrophilic ointments.
analysis: Hydrophobic ointments are known for their occlusive properties due to their ability to form a barrier on the skin, preventing moisture loss. In contrast, hydrophilic ointments and creams tend to be less occlusive as they contain water, which can evaporate and does not provide the same level of barrier protection. Therefore, among the options provided, hydrophobic ointments (option opa) are the most likely to have greater occlusivity.
